facts.text: Montgomery County, where Spencerville sits, was carved out of Frederick County in 1838 and named after Revolutionary War Major General Richard Montgomery.
The Metropolitan Branch of the Baltimore & Ohio Railroad once ran right through Montgomery County, linking Washington, D.C., to Point of Rocks and passing near Spencerville.
Spencerville lies just one mile north of Cloverly, placing it close to the bustling Washington, D.C., metropolitan area.
Paleo‑Indians first settled the Spencerville area, living in small semi‑nomadic groups that hunted large game like bison and mammoths.
Archaeologists have uncovered pottery shards and broken arrowheads near the current National Institutes of Health property, evidence of Late Woodland Period villagers.
Sargent Shriver, a native of Montgomery County, became the first director of the Peace Corps, a role that put the county on the national stage.
